questions.q: What does a Python function return if it has no `return` statement at all?
questions.explain: A function without an explicit return statement implicitly returns None.

questions.q: In `def call_model(prompt, temperature=0.7, max_tokens=500):`, what does the default value let you do?
options: Call the function without providing temperature or max_tokens, and Python uses the defaults
Force every caller to provide all three arguments
Nothing — defaults are purely documentation and have no runtime effect
Change the function's name at call time
questions.explain: Parameters with defaults become optional — the caller can omit them and the default value is used.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say keyword arguments matter for AI engineering specifically?
options: Because AI SDKs don't support any arguments at all
Because positional arguments are not allowed in Python
Because keyword arguments run faster than positional ones
Because real AI SDKs expect calls to be made this way, and it's self-documenting and order-independent
questions.explain: Naming arguments like prompt= and temperature= matches how real AI provider SDKs are typically called.

questions.q: What does *args collect inside a function definition?
options: Any number of extra positional arguments, as a tuple
Nothing — *args is not valid Python syntax
questions.explain: *args gathers any extra positional arguments passed to the function into a tuple.

questions.q: What does `valid, length = check_response("Hello!")` demonstrate, if check_response returns `is_valid, length`?
options: check_response must be called twice to get both values
This is invalid syntax and will raise an error
Python functions can only ever return a single value
A Python function can return multiple values at once, packaged as a tuple and unpacked on assignment
questions.explain: Returning comma-separated values packages them as a tuple, which can be unpacked into multiple variables at once.
